title: Staged regional degrade and soft circuit for 429s/timeouts with per-tenant adaptive cooldown
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a multi-stage automatic fallback and circuit system that reacts to 429 spikes, request timeouts, and elevated error rates with regional awareness and per-tenant adaptive cooldowns. The goal is to preserve global latency SLOs while minimizing customer-visible errors and avoiding full hard failovers that harm downstream UX. This ticket covers policy definition, runtime guard rails, telemetry, and a gradual rollout plan.
background: Recent incidents and stress tests exposed oscillation where global fallback policies tripped aggressively for a few noisy tenants or transient region-level congestion. Existing heuristics are binary (open/closed) and lack per-tenant memory and staged degradation. We need a smoother, signal-rich approach that enables: 1) soft degradation actions (reduce burst QPS, route to lighter model variant, enable aggressive cache reuse), 2) staged circuit opens with hysteresis, and 3) tenant-aware decay windows so noisy clients are quarantined while the fleet stabilizes.
goals: 1) Reduce end-user 5xx/timeout exposures during regional overloads by 60% in canary traffic. 2) Prevent global routing oscillations caused by single-tenant spikes. 3) Provide observability to understand why a tenant was degraded and what action was taken.
proposed_design: Policy surface: define a three-stage action set: PASSIVE (no routing changes, increased sampling + short-term token-backpressure), SOFT_DEGRADE (reduce per-tenant concurrency, route X% of requests to fallback model variant, enable KV prefix reuse), HARD_CIRCUIT (route all traffic for tenant-region to restricted fallback pool and impose strict QPS caps). Triggers: sliding-window sensor fusion of 429 rate, p95 latency timeouts, and absolute error-rate threshold. Each metric contributes to a 'trip score' with configurable weights. Staging: score thresholds for SOFT_DEGRADE and HARD_CIRCUIT include hysteresis and minimum stay durations. Per-tenant cooldown: exponential decay with a base window and tenant-specific multiplier derived from historical instability. Regional gating: policies evaluated per region and can cascade to adjacent regions if capacity-constrained. Interventions: prefer model variant fallback (quantized/cheaper) before full circuit. Control plane: expose per-tenant policy overrides and manual release. Runtime: lightweight policy evaluator in router process, with authoritative decisions persisted to regional control-plane cache to avoid split-brain.
rollout_plan: 1) Unit tests + simulation harness (offline replay of production traces) to validate trip score behavior. 2) Canary in EDU region for low-risk tenants (1% traffic). 3) Expand to 10% with strict observability and a rollback monitor. 4) Region-by-region ramp with kill-switch. 5) Post-rollout audit and tuning cycle. Each step gated by acceptance criteria and can be reverted within 10 minutes via console toggle.
telemetry_requirements: Emit trip_score and contributing signals per evaluation (429_rate, p95_latency, error_rate) as tags
Log action transitions (PASSIVE->SOFT_DEGRADE->HARD_CIRCUIT) with timestamps and actor (auto/manual)
Per-tenant per-region counters for degraded_request_count and fallback_variant_ratio
Expose dashboard with heatmap of active degradations and per-tenant cooldown windows
Alert when >0.5% of active tenants escalate to HARD_CIRCUIT within 5 minutes
acceptance_criteria: Simulator shows >60% reduction in end-user 5xx/timeouts for targeted overload scenarios
Canary traffic shows no regression in median latency and acceptable increase in cost per token (<8%)
Telemetry contains trip_score and full action history for every degraded request
Runbook updated with clear rollback steps and SLO impact table
Feature flag guarded and rollouts reversible from console
qa_steps: Create synthetic tenants that generate controlled 429/timeouts and verify staged progression
Replay historical incident trace and validate that policy would have chosen SOFT_DEGRADE vs HARD_CIRCUIT correctly
End-to-end smoke: request flows through router->model variant, verify headers show fallback reason tags
Chaos test: inject region-level latency and ensure neighbor-region gating doesn't cause global oscillation
risks: Incorrect weighting could cause premature hard circuits and customer disruption
Instrumentation overhead in router could add allocator pressure — must be bounded
Per-tenant cooldown tuning requires historical data; cold tenants may be misclassified
notes: Design reviewed with Platform and SRE. Need final sign-off from Privacy for per-tenant metrics retention. Suggest a short A/B test comparing fallback-to-quantized-model vs fallback-to-dedicated-fallback-pool for cost/quality tradeoffs.
